about.title: About me
paragraphs: PhD in Psychology from the Universitat de València (thesis defended December 16, 2025), awarded the highest distinction of Summa Cum Laude with International Mention for the dissertation "Chronic low back pain through the lens of positive body image: The role of functionality appreciation."

My predoctoral training was funded by an FPU grant (FPU20/05798, Ministry of Science, Innovation and Universities, 2021-2025) within the R&D project CLEVER ("Changing Low Back Pain Employing Virtual Enhanced Reality"), led by Dr. Rosa Mª Baños Rivera. Since February 2026 I have been a postdoctoral researcher in digital health at Adhera Health (Valencia), on the DALIA project, focused on data-driven personalization of a digital health solution for family caregivers of children with chronic conditions.

I am the author of 10 articles in JCR-indexed journals (mostly Q1), first author on 2 of them, and I have contributed to more than 20 national and international conferences — including presentations in the United States, Canada, France, the Netherlands and Spain.

I combine this research profile with an uncommon technical background for psychology: I hold a Higher Technician qualification in Multiplatform Application Development (average grade: 9, CEEDCV) and specific training in data analysis (R, Python, SQL, Excel, machine learning). I built AulaMetrics, a full Odoo/Python/PostgreSQL platform for psychosocial assessment in schools, validated with real school counsellors. I completed international research stays at the Université du Québec en Outaouais (Canada) and Universidade Lusófona (Lisbon, Portugal), and taught 90 hours at the Universitat de València in Psychology and Criminology, with student evaluations of 4.77-4.80/5.

items.name: AulaMetrics
items.tagline: A full psychosocial assessment and educational data analytics platform for schools, built on Odoo.

problem.title: The problem
problem.description: Spanish schools routinely need to run standardized psychosocial assessments (well-being, risk indicators) but typically lack a system to schedule them, collect anonymous responses at scale, analyze results, and flag risk automatically — counsellors are left doing this manually with spreadsheets.

solution.title: The solution
solution.description: AulaMetrics is a complete module built on Odoo 17 Community Edition that lets schools schedule standardized evaluations, collect anonymous responses through unique tokens, automatically analyze results with risk detection, and generate role-differentiated dashboards and reports for administrators, counsellors, tutors and school leadership.

features.title: Modular 3-layer architecture
features.description: Presentation, application and data layers with a purpose-built entity-relationship model: academic groups, evaluations, questionnaires, participations, alert thresholds, alerts and metrics.

features.title: Privacy & security by design
features.description: Four-level role system (administrator, counsellor, tutor, school leadership) with row-level access rules in Odoo, aggregated-data anonymization for tutors/leadership, GDPR/LOPDGDD-aware handling of minors' data, a session-less public portal secured with UUID v4 tokens, and HTML sanitization against XSS.

features.title: Validated with real school counsellors
features.description: Demo and feedback sessions with practicing counsellors at Spanish public schools drove a significant refactor of the scoring engine — adding multi-scale support per questionnaire (e.g. SDQ, SWLS) — plus a new case-tracking and internal messaging module.

features.title: Production-ready deployment
features.description: Containerized with Docker Compose (Odoo + PostgreSQL) on a Linux server, with a documented production plan including an Nginx reverse proxy and HTTPS.

dataAnalystNote.title: Why this matters for data analysis
dataAnalystNote.description: AulaMetrics is an end-to-end applied data engineering project — from the data model and collection to the analytics engine and visualization — built on a domain (psychosocial well-being in schools) directly connected to my research specialty. It reflects the same pipeline thinking I apply in quantitative research, taken all the way to production software.
